solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pleaded to adopt bird with curved limbs

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it into your household, so one word is taken inside the other

parts.note: begged is a synonym of pleaded

explanation.surface: Someone begs to take in a bird whose legs are crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adopt' reads as taking in a pet, but here it means one word swallows the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-legged describes legs that bend outward at the knee, so the limbs are curved.

clue.text: Youngster left to cause confusion

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A child abandoned in order to create chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Babel, from the biblical tower, means a confused noise of many voices.

clue.text: Call for hostilities with tirade

parts.note: war is a state of hostilities

explanation.surface: Someone demands war in an angry speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to justify or require it, as a situation calls for action.

clue.text: Choose part of film containing limitless vice — it's a shocker!

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the film word wraps round the shortened one
limitless means without its edges, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a reel is a section of film

explanation.surface: Pick a racy scene from a film about vice; it's scandalous!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocker' sounds like a scandal but means something that gives electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric eel is a South American fish that stuns prey with powerful electric discharges.

clue.text: Man's inheritance supports party, a brilliant gathering

parts.note: a gala is a festive party
males inherit an X and a Y chromosome

explanation.surface: A man's inheritance pays for a party, a dazzling get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supports' puts XY beneath GALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Galaxy also means an assembly of brilliant or famous people, a figurative use of a star system.

clue.text: Mysterious body of sailor found beneath 500 ships

explanation.surface: A sailor's corpse discovered under hundreds of vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'found beneath' places TAR under D and ARKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark star is a hypothetical celestial body giving off little or no light, hence mysterious.

clue.text: Tricks mum by returning cigarette

definitions.note: plural noun for a mass noun: conjuring tricks collectively

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Mum performs tricks by bringing back a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is the art of conjuring illusions, the stuff of a performer's tricks.

clue.text: Brit head over heels for messy hairdo

indicators.note: head over heels means upside down, which in a down clue turns the word round

parts.note: pom is Australian slang for a British person

explanation.surface: A Brit falls madly in love with an untidy haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: POM upside down gives MOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mop of hair is a thick untidy mass of it.

clue.text: Tear in limb upset man-eating monster

indicators.note: in places one word inside another
upset means turned over, which in a down clue reverses the word

explanation.surface: A torn, upset limb belongs to a man-eating beast.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'upset' turns a word upside down, which reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grendel is the monster in Beowulf who devours warriors in the mead hall.

clue.text: Drink loads, in conclusion

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: a coda is the concluding passage of a piece

explanation.surface: To finish, have plenty to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In conclusion' looks like a closing phrase, but 'in' is the signal and 'conclusion' is a musical ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet vanilla-flavoured fizzy soft drink.

clue.text: Gym equipment advocates reduced stomach

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
belly is another word for stomach

explanation.surface: Lawyers who pump iron trim their stomachs with gym kit.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR plus BELLY without its last letter gives BARBELL. Barristers in Britain are collectively called the Bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is a long weightlifting bar loaded with plates, standard kit in a gym.

clue.text: Filled theatre with rented audience in the end

parts.note: rep, short for repertory, is a kind of theatre

indicators.note: in the end points to the closing letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: A theatre is packed by an audience who hired their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full to capacity, synonymous with filled.

clue.text: King cut grassy meadow

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A monarch mows a grassy field.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAR loses his last letter to give LEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic term for an open area of grassland or pasture.

clue.text: Edited the exams to cover historic card game

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so the rearranged letters enclose another word
edited text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: old is a synonym of historic

explanation.surface: Someone revises old exam papers that cover the history of a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas hold 'em is the most popular variety of poker, a card game.

clue.text: Old patent getting Hello in a bad place

parts.note: patent means obvious, as does overt

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: hell is the worst place of all

explanation.surface: An old patent greets a grim location.
explanation.walkthrough: Patent here is the adjective meaning plain to see, not a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the hill is an idiom for past one's prime, getting old.

clue.text: Become stupid, briefly, like Frankenstein?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: go means become, as in go mad

explanation.surface: Turning dim-witted, a bit like Frankenstein's lumbering creation.
explanation.walkthrough: GO plus THICK without its last letter. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein is a classic Gothic novel, the horror genre of gloomy castles and monsters.

clue.text: Toledo ports agree to box up creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top
to box means to enclose, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: the run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: Spanish ports agree to cage a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Toledo is inland, so the surface is fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropod is a mollusc such as a snail or slug, a kind of creature.

clue.text: Move to a lower place in Belgium

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them about, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: Someone relocates to a lower-lying spot in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one instruction to relocate, but its first word is the signal and the next three words are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is a Belgian town south of Brussels, site of Napoleon's 1815 defeat.

clue.text: Fish doctor's opening strange piece of kit

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A doctor's first strange fishing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum meaning strange is old-fashioned British slang. A drum kit is a set of drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass drum is the large drum at the base of a drummer's kit.

clue.text: Second video game about European astronaut

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: about means around, so the game's name surrounds one letter

parts.note: Pac-Man is a classic arcade video game
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A second arcade game about a European space traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: S then PACMAN wrapped round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaceman is an informal word for someone who travels into space, an astronaut.

clue.text: Trains a poorly skilled worker

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone trains a craftsman badly.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson working skilfully with their hands.

clue.text: Layers of desserts from the east — Arabia primarily

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left
primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter

explanation.surface: Layered sweets imported from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are horizontal layers, especially of rock in geology.

clue.text: Generally, a promotion includes rug with one-third off

indicators.note: includes means holds within

parts.note: a sale is a promotion in a shop

indicators.note: removing a third of a three-letter word drops one letter, here the last

explanation.surface: A sale on rugs, usually a third off.
explanation.walkthrough: RUG has three letters, so a third off removes one.
explanation.definitionFit: As a rule is an idiom for usually, in general.

clue.text: 13 dads and a singer

definitions.note: cross-reference to 13 down, OVER THE HILL

explanation.surface: Old fathers and a singing performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 means the answer to 13 down, used here as the definition. A singer in crosswords is often a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it and over the hill are both idioms for too old to manage things.

clue.text: Earnest talk disturbed cold-blooded creature

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A serious conversation is interrupted by a heartless person.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold-blooded reads as callous, but here it is literal: reptiles cannot regulate their body heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a venomous reptile, and reptiles are cold-blooded animals.

clue.text: Towards the back of vessel, not the front

indicators.note: not the front tells you to drop the opening letter

parts.note: a raft is a simple vessel

explanation.surface: Heading to the stern of a boat, away from the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: RAFT without its first letter gives AFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical term for at or towards the stern, the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Run into nurse and get a lot of attention

indicators.note: into means going inside the next word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A nurse gets famous after running into someone.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: On social media a topic that trends is one getting a surge of attention.

clue.text: Regret returning to follow former chemist

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: Regret comes back to haunt a former chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist behind pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: One steering to avoid hard wooden thing

indicators.note: to avoid something is to leave it out

parts.note: the helm is the steering gear, or the one steering
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A helmsman dodges something hard and wooden.
explanation.walkthrough: HELM without H gives ELM.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm is a tree, and trees are made of wood.

clue.text: People surrounding United Nations official once

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so one word wraps round the other

explanation.surface: A crowd surrounds a former UN official.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribune was an elected official in ancient Rome who protected the plebeians.

clue.text: Material that's dangerous to walk over backwards?

indicators.note: backwards means read the word from its end to its start

parts.note: ground that is mined has explosives buried in it

explanation.surface: A fabric so hazardous it can only be crossed walking in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: MINED reversed gives DENIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric, a material used for jeans.

clue.text: Music fan ran into a show outside hotel

indicators.note: outside means around, so one word is placed on either side of a letter

parts.note: to lead the way is to show it
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A music lover bumped into a show outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Show means lead, as in show someone the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A metalhead is a devotee of heavy metal music.
